title: Reality Fracture | Episode 5: I Don't Need to Convince You

entities.name: The Theorist
entities.description: The clinical remnant of Jace, a utilitarian academic who beats his old friends with mind magic and finally learns he can simply command them.

entities.name: Vraska
entities.description: A gorgon planeswalker, Jace's beloved, who confronts the Theorist three times and calls him a monster before meeting Tam.

entities.name: Chandra Nalaar
entities.description: A pyromancer planeswalker paralyzed by indecision in the Theorist's attack.

entities.name: Ajani Goldmane
entities.description: A leonin planeswalker whose language the Theorist steals, leaving him speaking only Greek.

entities.name: Garruk Wildspeaker
entities.description: A huge planeswalker druid whose muscles the Theorist makes spasm and weaken.

entities.name: Tam
entities.description: An artificial gorgon made by Jace, who secretly helps Vraska and heals the others.

entities.name: Professor Opal
entities.description: The Echoverse's healer version of Liliana, who cheerfully watches the allies recover.

entities.name: Jace Beleren
entities.description: The whole planeswalker mind-mage that Vraska loved and who died and rebuilt himself in the Meditation Realm.

entities.name: Ranna Beleren
entities.description: Jace's mother, who sent a horseshoe to him.

entities.name: Pewter
entities.description: Jace's childhood horse, whose loss inspired the first illusion he made.

entities.name: Jadzi
entities.description: The oracle held captive by the Theorist.

entities.name: Liliana Vess
entities.description: The original necromancer whom Tam plans to get for backup.

entities.name: Loot
entities.description: A small creature in Jace and Vraska's family.

entities.name: Nicol Bolas
entities.description: A dragon who used the Meditation Realm to craft himself in his image.

entities.name: Ugin
entities.description: The spirit dragon who rebuilt himself from the Meditation Realm's power, a method Jace imitates.

entities.name: The Meditation Realm
entities.description: The place that held Jace's shattered selves together and let him craft a body.

entities.name: Hexhaven Academy
entities.description: The tower made of Jace's memories, containing his sanctum.

entities.name: The Sanctum
entities.description: The Theorist's chamber ringed with mage-rings.

entities.name: Chamber of the Guildpact
entities.description: A Ravnican chamber whose apartment Jace's pocket plane replicates.

entities.name: The Echoverse
entities.description: The Theorist's new Multiverse.

entities.name: The Belligerent
entities.description: A ship on which Jace once gave Vraska a hurt look.

events.summary: Vraska and her allies burst into the sanctum and Garruk, Chandra and Ajani collapse asleep at the Theorist's snap while Vraska stays standing.
events.quote: The four of them burst into his sanctum, and half a second later, three hit the floor.

events.summary: Vraska asks the Theorist to stop and gives him the horseshoe from his mother, which he drops, recalling the illusion of his childhood horse Pewter.
events.quote: how in the dark of night the child that was Jace snuck down and created a copy of Pewter to love with his whole heart.

events.summary: The Theorist insists he cannot be stopped, and Vraska asks how many will die.
Vraska tells him he is a killer who will murder billions, and he wipes her memory and sends the four out.
events.quote: her memory of the last few minutes is resting in the Theorist's hand.

events.summary: On the second attempt the Theorist freezes the group and shares a memory of how he rebuilt himself after dying.
events.quote: It is the day after he died. He is now they, and they have shattered.

events.summary: In the memory, Jace shapes a body from the Meditation Realm, imitating Ugin, and pours his fractured selves into it.
events.quote: shaping a body from the inherent power of this place and pouring his fractured selves inside.

events.summary: Jace creates a pocket plane and uses a mirror spell to make a person, Tam, from a wisp of himself.
events.quote: A person, or rather a person-shaped miasma of blue, emerges.

events.summary: The Theorist cannot remember why he made Tam, saying only that she is important and must be protected, and wipes their memories again.
events.quote: I made a person, but this part of me does not remember why. She must be protected.

events.summary: On the third attempt Vraska says he will not convince them, and the Theorist realizes he can command them instead.
events.quote: "I don't need to convince you, " he commands, dark and gentle.

events.summary: He orders the others to stop each other, and they fight until he calls it off.
The Theorist disables Chandra's decision-making, ruins Garruk's muscles and steals Ajani's language.
events.quote: The Theorist reaches inside Ajani's mind and snatches away an entire language.

events.summary: Vraska tells him she hates what he has become, and he sends her to sleep and wipes their minds, leaving only the knowledge that he cannot be defeated.
events.quote: I cannot be defeated by you.

events.summary: Vraska realizes they only fought the Theorist, the worst part of Jace.
events.quote: "That's not Jace," Vraska concludes with a sick roil of her guts. "It's just what's left."

events.summary: Vraska sees Tam in a hallway and recognizes who she is.
Tam warns Vraska that the Theorist can only be beaten by a telepath and says the tower is made of his memories; she tells her to rescue Jadzi.
events.quote: "It isn't worth it to fight him directly. You need to rescue Jadzi before he can use her."

events.summary: Tam heals the injured allies, restoring Garruk's muscles and Ajani's speech.
events.quote: Her eyes light up with blue, and after a long minute, both Chandra and Garruk relax.

events.summary: Vraska realizes Jace knows he is going to die.
events.quote: Jace knows he is going to die.

relations.note: Jace made Tam through a mirror spell in a pocket plane.
relations.quote: He pulls it out of the mirror, gasping with effort

relations.note: Vraska loved Jace and is called the woman who would be his wife.
relations.quote: The woman who would be his wife only stares.

relations.note: Vraska calls him a monster and says she hates what he became.
relations.quote: "You are the worst part of the best man,"
"Your mother asked me to give you this."

relations.note: Tam warns and helps Vraska against her maker.

relations.quote: The druid's axe clatters to the ground, his fingers too weak to hold it.
